title: Normalized ordinary derived evaluations for opposite signed integral lines
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E$ be a finite-dimensional field extension of $\mathbb Q_\ell$, and let $X$ be a scheme. Write $R$ for the completed integral coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site of $X$, and let $L$ be an $R$-module sheaf locally free of rank one. Use the signed powers, ordinary tensor functors $T_m$, sheaf evaluations and representative formula of [def-pur-integral-line-reduction-data]. Suppose a family $e$ of opposite-line evaluation isomorphisms satisfies EvaluationFormula: multiplication at exponent zero and functional evaluation for positive and negative exponents. For every integer $m$, there exist natural isomorphisms $v:T_m\mathbin{\cdot}T_{-m}\cong1$ and $w:T_{-m}\mathbin{\cdot}T_m\cong1$ on the entire unbounded derived category of $R$-modules, where functors are composed in their displayed order. They satisfy DerivedEvaluationFormula for $e(m)$ and reverseEvaluation$(e,m)$ respectively: on every admissible K-flat flat-term representative, their components are the localized chain cancellations $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)\mapsto e(y,z)x$ through the recorded representative comparisons. For every unbounded derived object $K$, $T_m(v_K^{-1})\,;\,w_{T_m(K)}=1_{T_m(K)}$. There are no completeness, constructibility, residue-characteristic or finite-reduction hypotheses or conclusions.

proof.text: Apply the chain cancellation theorem to the given normalized sheaf evaluations. It gives natural isomorphisms a and b between the two composite total-tensor functors on all complexes and the identity, their generator formulas and the first chain triangle identity. No localization or choice of a derived tensor model occurs in this step.

Signed powers are locally free of rank one. The line-unbounded theorem supplies K-flatness of their degree-zero complexes. Apply ringedTensorComparison_extension to the recorded closed tensor structure and its CoefficientTensorModels. Specializing the right factor to each degree-zero line gives natural isomorphisms c: Q followed by ordinary(m) ≅ chainTensor(m) followed by Q on every complex. The both-K-flat normalization and the definition of integralLineRepresentativeIso identify c on each good representative with the inverse of that recorded representative comparison.

Descend a and b through Q with c and d by the existing localizedCancellation construction in LineUnboundedDerivedTensor. Its component formula is G(c) followed by d followed by Q(a). The comparison for an iterated representative is d inverse followed by G(c inverse), directly from the definition of integralLineRepresentativeIso and functoriality of the recorded tensor. Cancelling these isomorphisms gives the representative equation Q(a), respectively Q(b); their chain generator formulas prove the two DerivedEvaluationFormula clauses. The existing localizedCancellation_triangles lemma descends the first chain triangle by localization faithfulness, yielding the required equation on every derived object.

lean.statement:
theorem integral_line_normalized_evaluations
    (L : scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X) [L.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1]
    (e : Evaluations l E X L) (he : EvaluationFormula l E X L e) (m : ℤ) :
    ∃ (v : ordinary l E X L m ⋙ ordinary l E X L (-m) ≅ 𝟭 (D.{u, u} l E X none))
      (w : ordinary l E X L (-m) ⋙ ordinary l E X L m ≅ 𝟭 (D.{u, u} l E X none)),
      DerivedEvaluationFormula l E X L m (-m) (e m) v ∧
      DerivedEvaluationFormula l E X L (-m) m (reverseEvaluation l E X L e m) w ∧
      ∀ K : D.{u, u} l E X none,
        (ordinary l E X L m).map (v.inv.app K) ≫
          w.hom.app ((ordinary l E X L m).obj K) = 𝟙 _
